Launch the interactive GLASS download interface

Source: R/shiny_launcher.R
glass_app.Rd

Starts a local 'shiny' app with a 'leaflet' map: switch between a roam mode (free pan/zoom, no drawing) and a draw mode with a button, then click twice on the map in draw mode to frame your region of interest as a rectangle; pick a verified product variant and date range, preview the file manifest, then batch-download with glass_fetch() in one click.

Usage

glass_app(port = getOption("shiny.port"))

Arguments

port

Port for the shiny server (see shiny::runApp()).

Value

Returns invisibly when the app stops.

Details

The app is thin: everything happens through the package functions, so the same workflow is available non-interactively via glass_fetch(). The download directory can be picked with the built-in, in-page directory browser (package 'shinyFiles'; no native modal, works in RStudio's Viewer pane and in any browser); without 'shinyFiles' the path can simply be typed in. A progress bar tracks each file during the batch download.

After a download, the map-header controls overlay a downsampled preview of the downloaded granules (fill/scale from the registry, multi-tile mosaics, cropped to the ROI and reprojected to EPSG:4326). Previously downloaded data can be brought in without re-downloading with the "Scan Import" button, which opens the same directory browser and recognizes GLASS granules by naming/code; the preview shows the first SDS layer of multi-band products. Requires 'shiny' and 'leaflet' (Suggested dependencies) to be installed. Base maps default to an unbiased Esri World Imagery layer; an Amap street layer is optional but uses GCJ-02 coordinates, so it is offset by roughly 500 meters from WGS84.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
glass_app()
} # }
